edition.locus: Gebhardt III.V (the heaven question; the common sentence)

source_text: Ὁ ἔπαρχος λέγει πρὸς τὸν Ἰουστῖνον· Ἄκουε, ὁ λεγόμενος λόγιος καὶ νομίζων ἀληθινοὺς εἰδέναι λόγους. Ἐὰν μαστιγωθεὶς ἀποκεφαλισθῇς, πέπεισαι ὅτι μέλλεις ἀναβαίνειν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἐλπίζω ἕξειν αὐτοῦ τὰ δώματα, ἐὰν ὑπομείνω ταῦτα. Οἶδα γὰρ πᾶσι τοῖς οὕτω βιώσασι παραμένειν τὸ θεῖον χάρισμα μέχρι τῆς ἐκπληρώσεως τοῦ παντὸς κόσμου. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Σὺ οὖν ὑπονοεῖς ὅτι ἀναβήσῃ εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, ἀμοιβὰς τινας ἀποληψόμενος; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐχ ὑπονοῶ, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπίσταμαι καὶ πεπληροφόρημαι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Τὸ λοιπὸν ἔλθωμεν εἰς τὸ προκείμενον καὶ κατεπεῖγον πρᾶγμα. Συνελθόντες οὖν ὁμοθυμαδὸν θύσατε τοῖς θεοῖς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐδεὶς εὖ φρονῶν ἀπὸ εὐσεβείας εἰς ἀσέβειαν μεταπίπτει. Ὁ Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Εἰ μὴ πείθεσθε, τιμωρηθήσεσθε ἀνηλεῶς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἃν εὐχῆς ἔχωμεν διὰ τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τιμωρηθέντες σωθῆναι, ὅτι τοῦτο ἡμῖν σωτηρία καὶ παρρησία γενήσεται ἐπὶ τοῦ φοβερωτέρου καὶ παγκοσμίου βήματος τοῦ δεσπότου ἡμῶν καὶ σωτῆρος. Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ μάρτυρες εἶπον· Ποίει ὃ θέλεις. Ἡμεῖς γὰρ Χριστιανοί ἐσμεν καὶ εἰδώλοις οὐ θύομεν. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος ἀπεφήνατο λέγων· Οἱ μὴ βουληθέντες θῦσαι τοῖς θεοῖς καὶ εἶξαι τῷ τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος προστάγματι μαστιγωθέντες ἀπαχθήτωσαν, κεφαλικὴν ἀποτιννύντες δίκην κατὰ τὴν τῶν νόμων ἀκολουθίαν.
pass_a_gloss: The prefect speaks to Justin, calling him learned and supposing to know true doctrines, and asks if after scourging and beheading he is convinced he will go up into heaven. Justin answers he hopes to have his dwellings if he endures these things, for he knows the divine gift abides for all who so lived until the fulfillment of the whole world. Rusticus the prefect asks if then he supposes he will ascend into the heavens to receive some rewards. Justin answers he does not suppose but knows and is fully assured. Rusticus the prefect says let them come to the subject at hand and urgent matter, and commands them to come together of one accord and sacrifice to the gods. Justin says no one of sound mind falls from piety to impiety. Rusticus says unless they obey they will be punished without mercy. Justin says what we pray for is being punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ to be saved, because this will be salvation and boldness for us before the more fearful and universal tribunal of our Master and Savior. Likewise also the remaining martyrs said do what you wish, for we are Christians and do not sacrifice to idols. Rusticus the prefect gave sentence saying those who refused to sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the command of the emperor, after being scourged, are to be led away paying the capital penalty by beheading according to the order of the laws.
pass_b_english: The prefect said to Justin, Listen, you who are called learned and imagine that you know true teachings. If you are scourged and beheaded, are you persuaded that you will ascend into heaven. Justin said, I hope to possess his abodes, if I endure these things. For I know that the divine gift abides for all who have lived in this way, until the consummation of the whole world. The prefect Rusticus said, Then do you suppose that you will ascend into the heavens to receive some rewards. Justin said, I do not suppose, but I know and am fully assured.

The prefect Rusticus said, Then let us come to the matter proposed and urgent. Come together with one accord and sacrifice to the gods. Justin said, No one of sound mind falls away from piety into impiety. The prefect Rusticus said, Unless you obey, you shall be punished without mercy. Justin said, What we pray for is that, punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ, we may be saved, because this shall become for us salvation and boldness before the most fearful and universal tribunal of our Master and Savior. Likewise also the remaining martyrs said, Do what you will. For we are Christians and do not sacrifice to idols. The prefect Rusticus pronounced sentence, saying, Those who have refused to sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the command of the emperor, after being scourged, shall be led away, paying the capital penalty according to the course of the laws.

choices.term: Οὐχ ὑπονοῶ, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπίσταμαι καὶ πεπληροφόρημαι
choices.english: I do not suppose, but I know and am fully assured
choices.why: contrasts the prefect's ὑπονοεῖς with a progression from supposition to knowledge to settled conviction, so it must be stronger than mere opinion
rejected: I do not think, but I believe

choices.english: What we pray for is to be saved by being punished
choices.why: the clause states the martyrs' desire, with the participle giving the means or circumstance of salvation, not a conditional wish
rejected: If we might have a prayer to be saved

choices.why: formal judicial formula for execution, with δίκην as penalty owed and κεφαλικήν specifying death by beheading

variants: δώματα scripsi against δόγματα codd. (δόμαεα O): 'mansions' adopted (Jn 14:2 echo), not 'doctrines'.
